locator: I q.75 a.2 co.: Si igitur principium intellectuale haberet in se naturam alicuius corporis
interpretation: The conditional preceding the first conclusion says that having any bodily nature in the intellectual principle would prevent cognition of all bodies. The formal negative universal does not choose a particular unknowable nature. Its application to intellect is an open source commitment; the taste example is not encoded as a proof of it.
